points.text: Sponsors: Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) of Environment and Public Works; Mike Lee (R-Utah) and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) of Energy and Natural Resources.
The White House said the bill would “deliver transformative policies to lower Americans’ energy and housing costs”.
Language on wind and solar permits is still being negotiated with the White House. The sponsors expect amendments before the vote.
The House passed its own bill, the SPEED Act, 221-196 on December 18, 2025. The two chambers would have to agree on one text.

next.text: Senate cloture vote, about 5:30 p.m., on taking up H.R. 2347, the legislative vehicle for the bill. It is the Senate's first vote after the November 3 election.

headlines.title: Review deadlines
headlines.text: Sets 2-year EIS and 1-year assessment deadlines, followed by deadlines for agency decisions. Extensions and enforcement conditions apply; the travel sanction limits official trips beyond 25 miles after a qualifying deadline is 60 days overdue.

headlines.title: Lawsuit limits
headlines.text: Generally allows 150 days for NEPA challenges in a court of appeals, with direct-harm and conditional comment requirements. Limits remedies to remand, with a fix due within 180 days; preliminary injunctions remain available under specified conditions involving other law.

headlines.title: Permit certainty
headlines.text: Restricts interference with permits in effect on or after September 16, 2026, subject to listed exceptions including the holder’s request. If the agency fails to meet its burden in court, the sponsor is entitled to specified relief, including a court-determined 25 to 50 percent of incurred project costs not otherwise recovered.

headlines.title: Data center costs
headlines.text: Newly connected data-center loads of 20 megawatts or more must cover their incremental electricity costs. Previously approved service arrangements remain in effect. The bill recognizes state authority to require new generation.

headlines.title: Transmission siting
headlines.text: FERC can permit interstate lines of 230 kilovolts and up that states have not approved, after making required findings, and planning regions must plan lines with their neighbors.

headlines.title: Actions outside NEPA
headlines.text: Excludes specified loan-only actions, qualifying work in existing grid and pipeline corridors, and listed oil, gas and geothermal activities from NEPA. Each exclusion has its own scope and conditions.

headlines.title: Clean Water Act
headlines.text: Narrows state water-quality certification review and generally limits it to one year; extensions require written agreement. Extends nationwide permits to 10 years.

headlines.title: Endangered Species Act
headlines.text: Cuts the standard formal consultation period from 90 days to 60, with extension rules. Lets approved state programs assume specified consultation responsibilities; applicants can opt for federal consultation.

headlines.title: Historic preservation
headlines.text: Narrows the effects covered by historic-preservation review and sets deadlines. Adds a 150-day challenge window and limits remedies, with separate rules for missed deadlines.

headlines.title: Digital permitting
headlines.text: Requires a public tracker of defined transparency projects, and targets December 1, 2028 for an interagency ePermit system, to the maximum extent practicable.
